updates.note: Mistral has released the weights on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B), whose model card lists 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion counting embeddings and output layers, the figure Mistral's launch page now shows), and its [release post](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/) says the open model got three more weeks of reinforcement learning and now costs $0.70 per million input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens. Mistral says the released build scores 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, up from 28% in the preview, and the Artificial Analysis and Vals pages cited above now show results for the released model rather than the preview figures quoted here.

A third version of the RealCompanion preprint, [posted Oct. 8](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01780v3), adds Jiayi Yu and Eric Huang as authors and drops the sentence reporting that a language model matched writing samples to the right person 98% of the time; the [v2 text](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01780v2) cited here still contains it, and v3 gives no reason for the change. The paper is still not peer-reviewed.

The three GitHub URLs (allenv0/SCM, its LICENSE, homebrew-scm cask) returned 403 to curl and gh because this session's proxy blocks GitHub. WebFetch loaded the SCM repo page fine: it is public, MIT-licensed, still says Apple Silicon and macOS 12+, and the cask still clears the quarantine flag. Left as is.

Source 1 (Mistral launch page) was revised after publication without a changelog. It now says '52 billion active parameters' and lists $0.7 / $2.1 per million tokens, where the issue quotes 49 billion and $1.36 / $4.18. Willison's same-day post (source 5) confirms that 49B was the original figure, and the new Hugging Face model card shows both numbers are right: 49B active per token, 52B counting embeddings and output layers. Covered by the Mistral update note.

noChangeReasons: Mistral claims: the issue reported the preview figures accurately as of Oct 6 (Willison and the original fact-check confirm this). The open-weight release (Hugging Face card: 1T total, 49B active per token, weights not gated, 'Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license', a modified MIT license per Mistral) confirms the issue's size claim and does not contradict it. So it is logged as an update, not a correction, and the body was not edited.

Artificial Analysis now shows the released model at 26 on its index (median 23, 110M tokens, 'somewhat verbose'), and Vals shows 45.09% with Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 27.78%. These measure a different build and maybe a revised index, so the preview-era numbers in the body were not rewritten. The update note tells readers the pages have changed.
TechCrunch (4,000 GPUs, 'three weeks, after safety testing') and Willison ('6 months behind the frontier', 38 on AA, Large 3 at 9) have not changed and carry no correction notes.

RealCompanion: every other number cited from v2 (27,218 messages, 3.4%, 1.3%, 2,157, 95.9%, 2.2%, 0.530 AUROC, 60.8%, 546M tokens, 73%, 'seventy to eighty', 'imagine more') is unchanged in v3. OpenAlex and Crossref show no peer-reviewed version, and nothing on the arXiv page indicates a withdrawal, so claimStatus stays 'preprint'. The 98% figure's removal is logged as an update, not a correction, because the authors gave no reason and the cited v2 still supports the sentence.

The RealCompanion dataset page still says 'A person reviews every request' and requires the DUA. Its Hugging Face config shows gated:'auto', but it was last modified Oct 6, before publication, and the issue accurately quotes the page. No change.

SCM: there are no independent tests or new release notes. The repo page wording has shifted ('your media never leaves the machine') and the fetch summary did not show the midpoint-frame, 435MB and 480-570 ms lines. I could not confirm that through the blocked GitHub API, so the README-based caveats were left as published.
